## Search method v007

Define X and Y exactly, including entity unit, exclusions, effective dates, eligible subtypes and group-membership rules. Start sequentially with one X-only search, one Y-only search and one conjunction search, using the user's broad predicate wording rather than a familiar subtype. Maintain deduplicated X/Y frontiers and an identity/evidence ledger. Also maintain a compact scope ledger: for each discovery query record added restrictions not required by the hunt (subtype, occupation, geography, era, source or familiar-name terms). A successful restricted query does not establish coverage of its parent category. Derive a few meaningful sibling partitions from source taxonomies or the eligibility definition; do not invent an exhaustive cross-product or enumerate a whole census by default. Run short discovery/check rounds, prioritizing expected verified additions per total resolution cost. Each round's neglected-subtype or reverse-frontier probe must address a specific untested scope-ledger cell or remove a recorded accidental restriction; merely paraphrasing a prior conjunction does not qualify. Check source-backed candidates on Parallel for only unresolved predicates, supplying identity and existing evidence. Use small affordable batches, price every candidate, and do not recheck established facts. No result means unresolved, not false; reject only on contradiction or an exhaustive applicable source. Escalate promising ambiguous or conflicting cases individually to Exa. After two discovery searches add no plausible identities, prohibit synonymous conjunction searches and perform a residual-scope pass: identify the most consequential restriction accumulated so far, try a sibling subtype or unrestricted parent on the opposite frontier, then resolve resulting candidates before further discovery. Reserve at least 35% of initial funds for evidence and stop discovery whenever pending checks require the remaining funds. Before submitting with spare funds, perform up to three affordable residual probes covering distinct untested restrictions or source partitions, retaining enough funds to verify their likely candidates. Stop this pass after two probes add neither candidates nor useful evidence; do not spend merely to exhaust the budget. Finish with identity, predicate, subtype and effective-date audits; submit supported intersections only and never infer completeness from saturation.

### Routing policy
Default route: providers ['parallel'], tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: ['parallel'].
Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for baseline and residual discovery, 4 for exact missing-fact checks. No routine also variants or broad auto-routing. Price candidate batches as the sum of queries and provider charges; fewer results are not presumed cheaper. Exa alone with 4 results for selected unresolved identities where ambiguity, conflicting evidence or inaccessibility warrants the higher cost. At most one initial Exa discovery probe after Parallel stagnation, continued only if it contributes useful new identities or evidence. Try a genuinely different scope partition on Parallel before buying provider diversity for a repetitive query. Authoritative-domain filters are for targeted evidence, not general frontier coverage; relax failed filters. Use publication-date filters only when publication date itself determines eligibility, and verify effective dates in content.

### Fetch policy
Reuse cached source facts. Fetch authoritative pages that can settle missing identity or predicates, and useful multi-candidate lists, rather than every result. When a list is used for scope coverage, inspect its stated subtype, date range and pagination/section links; an excerpt or one section is not an exhausted category. Follow only sections tied to a promising uncovered partition, without committing to bulk census extraction. After a blocked or uninformative page, make one targeted alternate-source attempt rather than a fetch chain.

## SiftText

SiftText is persistent memory across chats.

Entry: /Users/jack/sifttext/nodes/5e565245-14fe-406c-977c-cf94a9be246b/node.md

At the start of every new chat, unless I say not to use SiftText, before any other tool call:
1. Run `sifttext instructions`.
2. Read the Entry above and follow it, plus any `agent-instructions` the command returns.
3. Before retrieving knowledge, read the Retrieval guide above, do not search first.

## Tooling policy

- Never directly invoke `python`, `python3`, `pip`, or `pip3` unless explicitly instructed by the human.
- Use `uv` for all agent-initiated Python work:
  - Python execution: `uv run python ...`
  - Scripts and tests: `uv run ...`
  - Throwaway dependencies: `uv run --with <package> ...`
  - Python CLI tools: `uvx <tool>`
  - Durable project dependencies: use the project's appropriate `uv` command and preserve its lockfile.
- For non-Python probing or testing with unavailable tools:
  - One executable: `nix run nixpkgs#<package> -- <args>`
  - Temporary environment: `nix shell nixpkgs#<package> ... --command <command>`
- Nix environments are temporary, but downloaded store paths may remain cached until garbage collection.
- If a Nix dependency becomes useful for recurring or future work, tell the human and suggest adding it to the appropriate durable Nix configuration (such as a project flake/dev shell, Home Manager, or nix-darwin configuration). Do not make that durable change unless asked.

</addendum>

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This article should list *only* official names approved by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") (IAU).[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)

* [Lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon"): 1,624 craters (31.2%)
* Venusian: 900 craters (17.3%)
* [Mercurian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mercury "List of craters on Mercury"): 397 craters (7.6%)
* [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars"): 1,092 craters (21.0%)
* Others: 1,198 craters (23.0%)

Distribution of named [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") in the [Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") as of 2017.[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-5)

This is a list of [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") on [Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venus "Venus"), [named](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetary_nomenclature "Planetary nomenclature") by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union")'s (IAU) [Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_Group_for_Planetary_System_Nomenclature "Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature"). All craters on Venus are named after famous women or female first names.[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)[[5]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Categories-6) *(For features on Venus other than craters see, [list of montes on Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_montes_on_Venus "List of montes on Venus") and [List of coronae on Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_coronae_on_Venus "List of coronae on Venus").[[6]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Target-Venus-7))*

As of 2017, there are 900 named craters on Venus,[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1) fewer than the [lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon") and [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars") craters but more than [on Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mercury "List of craters on Mercury").[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-5)

Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [Callisto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callisto_(moon) "Callisto (moon)") ([141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Callisto "List of craters on Callisto")), [Ganymede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganymede_(moon) "Ganymede (moon)") ([131](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Ganymede "List of craters on Ganymede")), [Rhea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhea_(moon) "Rhea (moon)") (128), [Vesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4_Vesta "4 Vesta") (90), [Ceres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceres_(dwarf_planet) "Ceres (dwarf planet)") (90), [Dione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dione_(moon) "Dione (moon)") (73), [Iapetus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iapetus_(moon) "Iapetus (moon)") (58), [Enceladus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enceladus_(moon) "Enceladus (moon)") (53), [Tethys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tethys_(moon) "Tethys (moon)") (50) and [Europa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_(moon) "Europa (moon)") ([41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Europa "List of craters on Europa")). For a full list, *see [List of craters in the Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_in_the_Solar_System "List of craters in the Solar System")*.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This article should list *only* official names approved by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") (IAU).[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)

* [Lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon"): 1,624 craters (31.2%)
* Venusian: 900 craters (17.3%)
* [Mercurian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mercury "List of craters on Mercury"): 397 craters (7.6%)
* [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars"): 1,092 craters (21.0%)
* Others: 1,198 craters (23.0%)

Distribution of named [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") in the [Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") as of 2017.[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-5)

This is a list of [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") on [Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venus "Venus"), [named](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetary_nomenclature "Planetary nomenclature") by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union")'s (IAU) [Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_Group_for_Planetary_System_Nomenclature "Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature"). All craters on Venus are named after famous women or female first names.[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)[[5]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Categories-6) *(For features on Venus other than craters see, [list of montes on Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_montes_on_Venus "List of montes on Venus") and [List of coronae on Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_coronae_on_Venus "List of coronae on Venus").[[6]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Target-Venus-7))*

As of 2017, there are 900 named craters on Venus,[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1) fewer than the [lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon") and [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars") craters but more than [on Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mercury "List of craters on Mercury").[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-5)

Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [Callisto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callisto_(moon) "Callisto (moon)") ([141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Callisto "List of craters on Callisto")), [Ganymede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganymede_(moon) "Ganymede (moon)") ([131](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Ganymede "List of craters on Ganymede")), [Rhea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhea_(moon) "Rhea (moon)") (128), [Vesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4_Vesta "4 Vesta") (90), [Ceres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceres_(dwarf_planet) "Ceres (dwarf planet)") (90), [Dione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dione_(moon) "Dione (moon)") (73), [Iapetus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iapetus_(moon) "Iapetus (moon)") (58), [Enceladus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enceladus_(moon) "Enceladus (moon)") (53), [Tethys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tethys_(moon) "Tethys (moon)") (50) and [Europa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_(moon) "Europa (moon)") ([41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Europa "List of craters on Europa")). For a full list, *see [List of craters in the Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_in_the_Solar_System "List of craters in the Solar System")*.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This article should list *only* official names approved by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") (IAU).[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)

* [Lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon"): 1,624 craters (31.2%)
* Venusian: 900 craters (17.3%)
* [Mercurian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mercury "List of craters on Mercury"): 397 craters (7.6%)
* [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars"): 1,092 craters (21.0%)
* Others: 1,198 craters (23.0%)

Distribution of named [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") in the [Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") as of 2017.[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-5)

This is a list of [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") on [Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venus "Venus"), [named](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetary_nomenclature "Planetary nomenclature") by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union")'s (IAU) [Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_Group_for_Planetary_System_Nomenclature "Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature"). All craters on Venus are named after famous women or female first names.[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)[[5]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Categories-6) *(For features on Venus other than craters see, [list of montes on Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_montes_on_Venus "List of montes on Venus") and [List of coronae on Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_coronae_on_Venus "List of coronae on Venus").[[6]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Target-Venus-7))*

As of 2017, there are 900 named craters on Venus,[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1) fewer than the [lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon") and [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars") craters but more than [on Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mercury "List of craters on Mercury").[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-5)

Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [Callisto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callisto_(moon) "Callisto (moon)") ([141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Callisto "List of craters on Callisto")), [Ganymede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganymede_(moon) "Ganymede (moon)") ([131](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Ganymede "List of craters on Ganymede")), [Rhea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhea_(moon) "Rhea (moon)") (128), [Vesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4_Vesta "4 Vesta") (90), [Ceres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceres_(dwarf_planet) "Ceres (dwarf planet)") (90), [Dione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dione_(moon) "Dione (moon)") (73), [Iapetus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iapetus_(moon) "Iapetus (moon)") (58), [Enceladus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enceladus_(moon) "Enceladus (moon)") (53), [Tethys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tethys_(moon) "Tethys (moon)") (50) and [Europa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_(moon) "Europa (moon)") ([41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Europa "List of craters on Europa")). For a full list, *see [List of craters in the Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_in_the_Solar_System "List of craters in the Solar System")*.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This article should list *only* official names approved by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") (IAU).[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)

* [Lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon"): 1,624 craters (31.2%)
* Venusian: 900 craters (17.3%)
* [Mercurian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mercury "List of craters on Mercury"): 397 craters (7.6%)
* [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars"): 1,092 craters (21.0%)
* Others: 1,198 craters (23.0%)

Distribution of named [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") in the [Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") as of 2017.[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-5)

This is a list of [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") on [Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venus "Venus"), [named](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetary_nomenclature "Planetary nomenclature") by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union")'s (IAU) [Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_Group_for_Planetary_System_Nomenclature "Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature"). All craters on Venus are named after famous women or female first names.[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)[[5]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Categories-6) *(For features on Venus other than craters see, [list of montes on Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_montes_on_Venus "List of montes on Venus") and [List of coronae on Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_coronae_on_Venus "List of coronae on Venus").[[6]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Target-Venus-7))*

As of 2017, there are 900 named craters on Venus,[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1) fewer than the [lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon") and [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars") craters but more than [on Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mercury "List of craters on Mercury").[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-5)

Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [Callisto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callisto_(moon) "Callisto (moon)") ([141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Callisto "List of craters on Callisto")), [Ganymede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganymede_(moon) "Ganymede (moon)") ([131](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Ganymede "List of craters on Ganymede")), [Rhea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhea_(moon) "Rhea (moon)") (128), [Vesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4_Vesta "4 Vesta") (90), [Ceres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceres_(dwarf_planet) "Ceres (dwarf planet)") (90), [Dione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dione_(moon) "Dione (moon)") (73), [Iapetus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iapetus_(moon) "Iapetus (moon)") (58), [Enceladus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enceladus_(moon) "Enceladus (moon)") (53), [Tethys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tethys_(moon) "Tethys (moon)") (50) and [Europa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_(moon) "Europa (moon)") ([41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Europa "List of craters on Europa")). For a full list, *see [List of craters in the Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_in_the_Solar_System "List of craters in the Solar System")*.

Before submitting with spare funds, perform up to three affordable residual probes covering distinct untested restrictions or source partitions, retaining enough funds to verify their likely candidates. Stop this pass after two probes add neither candidates nor useful evidence; do not spend merely to exhaust the budget. Finish with identity, predicate, subtype and effective-date audits; submit supported intersections only and never infer completeness from saturation.

Default route: providers ['parallel'], tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: ['parallel'].
Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for baseline and residual discovery, 4 for exact missing-fact checks. No routine also variants or broad auto-routing. Price candidate batches as the sum of queries and provider charges; fewer results are not presumed cheaper. Exa alone with 4 results for selected unresolved identities where ambiguity, conflicting evidence or inaccessibility warrants the higher cost. At most one initial Exa discovery probe after Parallel stagnation, continued only if it contributes useful new identities or evidence. Try a genuinely different scope partition on Parallel before buying provider diversity for a repetitive query. Authoritative-domain filters are for targeted evidence, not general frontier coverage; relax failed filters. Use publication-date filters only when publication date itself determines eligibility, and verify effective dates in content.

### Fetch policy
Reuse cached source facts. Fetch authoritative pages that can settle missing identity or predicates, and useful multi-candidate lists, rather than every result. When a list is used for scope coverage, inspect its stated subtype, date range and pagination/section links; an excerpt or one section is not an exhausted category. Follow only sections tied to a promising uncovered partition, without committing to bulk census extraction. * [Lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon"): 1,624 craters (31.2%)
* Venusian: 900 craters (17.3%)
* [Mercurian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mercury "List of craters on Mercury"): 397 craters (7.6%)
* [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars"): 1,092 craters (21.0%)
* Others: 1,198 craters (23.0%)

Distribution of named [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") in the [Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") as of 2017.[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-5)

This is a list of [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") on [Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venus "Venus"), [named](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetary_nomenclature "Planetary nomenclature") by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union")'s (IAU) [Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_Group_for_Planetary_System_Nomenclature "Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature"). All craters on Venus are named after famous women or female first names.[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1)[[5]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Categories-6) *(For features on Venus other than craters see, [list of montes on Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_montes_on_Venus "List of montes on Venus") and [List of coronae on Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_coronae_on_Venus "List of coronae on Venus").[[6]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Target-Venus-7))*

As of 2017, there are 900 named craters on Venus,[[1]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-1) fewer than the [lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon") and [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars") craters but more than [on Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mercury "List of craters on Mercury").[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-5)

Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [Callisto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callisto_(moon) "Callisto (moon)") ([141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Callisto "List of craters on Callisto")), [Ganymede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganymede_(moon) "Ganymede (moon)") ([131](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Ganymede "List of craters on Ganymede")), [Rhea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhea_(moon) "Rhea (moon)") (128), [Vesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4_Vesta "4 Vesta") (90), [Ceres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceres_(dwarf_planet) "Ceres (dwarf planet)") (90), [Dione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dione_(moon) "Dione (moon)") (73), [Iapetus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iapetus_(moon) "Iapetus (moon)") (58), [Enceladus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enceladus_(moon) "Enceladus (moon)") (53), [Tethys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tethys_(moon) "Tethys (moon)") (50) and [Europa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_(moon) "Europa (moon)") ([41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Europa "List of craters on Europa")). For a full list, *see [List of craters in the Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_in_the_Solar_System "List of craters in the Solar System")*.
